description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — July 26, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: QwenLM/qwen-code is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: QwenLM/qwen-code leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 24 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 24 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: QwenLM/qwen-code — 7 commits today and 3 same-day mapped articles, 30.7 below its current daily pace, with 6 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 85 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
earendil-works/pi — No same-day commit after 121 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: A live trust change needs a session boundary, not a wish
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code's public workspace-trust hot-reload change treats a changed trust policy as a runtime transition: it rebuilds workspace generations, reports reconciliation state, and makes affected daemon routes fail closed rather than leaving an existing task to continue against an ambiguous policy.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The source adds a daemon trust-policy monitor and reconciler, generation guards around workspace runtime work, route-level untrusted and generation-closed responses, and focused tests for policy changes, drains, retries, and in-flight state. That is an implementation contract for Qwen Code source, not evidence that every deployment has it.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Agent operators often treat a folder-trust or permission edit as a quiet configuration update. If a task, session, or tool route can outlive the change, the old authority may continue invisibly. A named generation boundary gives a system a place to stop, rebuild, and explain what changed before it performs more work.

actions.label: Audit a live policy change
actions.instruction: While a non-sensitive agent task is active, change one workspace trust or permission rule and verify that every tool route either receives the new policy through an explicit generation transition or fails closed with a visible reason. Capture the session, tool, and retry behaviour.

actions.label: Test the source boundary before relying on it
actions.instruction: Use an isolated test workspace to compare a trust-policy change before and during a task. Confirm that the observed build and configuration match the public source change, then check whether a blocked request and a clean restart leave an understandable audit trail.

receipts.title: feat(serve): Hot-reload workspace trust changes (#7268)
receipts.supports: Shows workspace runtime generations being rebuilt on trust-policy changes, fail-closed daemon-route handling, reconciliation status, and targeted monitor, guard, and route tests.

confidence.basis: The public commit message, implementation surface, and extensive focused tests agree on the trust-reconciliation and generation-boundary mechanism; the conclusion is confined to that Qwen Code source change.

dailyInsight.limitation: This is source-level evidence. It does not establish release inclusion, a deployed Qwen Code instance, the behaviour of a particular workspace configuration, or the correctness of every permission rule and recovery path.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if later source or tests show that a trust change can leave an old generation performing a tool action without an explicit policy check, if the guard is bypassed on a supported route, or if the change is reverted before release.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a tagged release and a public end-to-end test or operator report that changes trust during an active session and records the exact blocked, drained, restarted, and audit-visible outcomes.
